Consider the function \(y = {@yexpr@}\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). Its graph is shown below.

[[jsxgraph width="520px" height="320px"]] (function() { var a = {#a#}, fs = {#fs#}, amp = Math.abs(a), top = amp + 0.9; var f = function(t) { return fs === 1 ? a*Math.sin(t) : a*Math.cos(t); }; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.7, top, 2*Math.PI + 1.1, -top], axis:false, grid:false, keepaspectratio:false, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false}); for (var k = 1; k <= 4; k++) { b.create('segment', [[k*Math.PI/2, -amp - 0.3], [k*Math.PI/2, amp + 0.3]], {strokeColor:'#cfd8dc', strokeWidth:1, fixed:true, highlight:false}); } for (var j = -amp; j <= amp; j++) { if (j !== 0) { b.create('segment', [[0, j], [2*Math.PI, j]], {strokeColor:'#eceff1', strokeWidth:1, fixed:true, highlight:false}); } } b.create('arrow', [[-0.3, 0], [2*Math.PI + 0.6, 0]], {strokeColor:'#444', fixed:true, highlight:false}); b.create('arrow', [[0, -top + 0.2], [0, top - 0.1]], {strokeColor:'#444', fixed:true, highlight:false}); b.create('text', [2*Math.PI + 0.55, -0.25, 'x'], {fixed:true}); b.create('text', [0.08, top - 0.25, 'y'], {fixed:true}); ['π/2', 'π', '3π/2', '2π'].forEach(function(l, i) { var t = (i + 1)*Math.PI/2; b.create('segment', [[t, -0.08], [t, 0.08]], {strokeColor:'#444', fixed:true}); b.create('text', [t, -0.3, l], {fixed:true, anchorX:'middle', anchorY:'top', fontSize:12}); }); for (var m = -amp; m <= amp; m++) { if (m !== 0) { b.create('segment', [[-0.06, m], [0.06, m]], {strokeColor:'#444', fixed:true}); b.create('text', [-0.12, m, '' + m], {fixed:true, anchorX:'right', anchorY:'middle', fontSize:11}); } } b.create('functiongraph', [f, 0, 2*Math.PI], {strokeColor:'#1565c0', strokeWidth:3, fixed:true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

(a) Reading values from the graph

Step 1: find each point on the curve. Go up (or down) from each value of \(x\) to the curve, then across to the \(y\)-axis. You can check each reading with the equation: \(y\) is \({@a@}\) times the value of \([[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\).

\(x\)\(0\)\(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\)\(\pi\)\(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\)\(2\pi\)
\([[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\)\({@b1@}\)\({@b2@}\)\({@b3@}\)\({@b4@}\)\({@b5@}\)
\(y = {@yexpr@}\)\({@y1@}\)\({@y2@}\)\({@y3@}\)\({@y4@}\)\({@y5@}\)

So \(y = {@y1@}\), \({@y2@}\), \({@y3@}\), \({@y4@}\) and \({@y5@}\) at \(x = 0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\).

12 : -14], fontSize:11, color:'#c62828'}}); }); b.create('segment', [[0, amp], [2*Math.PI, amp]], {strokeColor:'#2e7d32', dash:2, fixed:true}); b.create('segment', [[0, -amp], [2*Math.PI, -amp]], {strokeColor:'#2e7d32', dash:2, fixed:true}); b.create('text', [2*Math.PI + 0.12, amp, 'max ' + amp], {fixed:true, color:'#2e7d32', fontSize:11, anchorY:'middle'}); b.create('text', [2*Math.PI + 0.12, -amp, 'min −' + amp], {fixed:true, color:'#2e7d32', fontSize:11, anchorY:'middle'}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

(b) Maximum and minimum values

Step 2: find the highest and lowest points. Since \(-1 \le [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x \le 1\), multiplying by \({@a@}\) gives values between \({@ymin@}\) and \({@ymax@}\). The highest point of the curve is at \(y = {@ymax@}\) and the lowest is at \(y = {@ymin@}\).[[if test="is(a<0)"]] Because \(a\) is negative, the graph is the graph of \(y = {@amp@}[[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\) reflected in the \(x\)-axis, so the maximum and minimum swap places, but their values are still \({@ymax@}\) and \({@ymin@}\).[[/if]]

Maximum value \(= {@ymax@}\), minimum value \(= {@ymin@}\).

(c) Amplitude and period

Step 3: the amplitude is the distance from the middle line \(y = 0\) to the maximum, which is half of the maximum minus the minimum:

\[ \text{amplitude} = \frac{{@ymax@} - ({@ymin@})}{2} = {@amp@}. \]

For \(y = a[[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\) the amplitude is \(|a| = {@amp@}\). It is always positive.

Step 4: the period is the length of one complete cycle before the graph repeats. The curve starts at \(({@0@}, {@y1@})\), goes through one full wave, and is back at the same height, moving the same way, at \(x = 2\pi\). So the period is \(2\pi\).

Final answers: (a) \({@y1@}, {@y2@}, {@y3@}, {@y4@}, {@y5@}\); (b) maximum \({@ymax@}\), minimum \({@ymin@}\); (c) amplitude \({@amp@}\), period \(2\pi\).
